questions.question: Which pattern do you want for dstrader-public going forward? (Affects this v5 push AND every future periodic sync.)

options.label: Drop required_status_checks from the ruleset (Recommended)
options.description: Keep: `deletion`, `non_fast_forward`, `required_linear_history`. Drop: `required_status_checks`. The real leak gate is the SOP audit chain + GitHub-side Secret Scanning + Push Protection (already enabled in Phase 4); the status-check rule was duplicating the gate at the wrong layer for a direct-push workflow. Worker PATCHes the ruleset, retries the push (now works), Phase E verifies, cleans up. Re-addable later if dstrader-public ever moves to PR-based syncs.

options.label: Switch dstrader-public to PR-based syncs
options.description: Drop the no-PRs convention for dstrader-public specifically (memory only applies to private dstrader). Each sync: worker creates a feature branch, opens a PR via `gh pr create`, lets the workflow run on the PR's merge candidate (check lands), then `gh pr merge --squash` or `--merge`. Higher operational complexity per sync but preserves the status-check gate.

options.label: Bypass-and-push pattern per sync
options.description: Each sync: worker PATCHes ruleset to set `enforcement: "disabled"`, pushes to main, PATCHes back to `"active"`. Trivial mechanics, but the disable-window is a soft spot every sync.

options.label: Add bypass_actors for this one push, then remove
options.description: Worker PATCHes ruleset to add `jdtogni78` to bypass_actors → push c2d27e6 to main → PATCH to remove. Same shape as the disable-and-re-enable pattern but uses the bypass mechanism. Each future sync repeats.

## Root cause found — ruleset config bug

The workflow_dispatch path worked perfectly (Steps 1–3 PASS): Secret Scan check landed on `c2d27e6` with conclusion=success. But the push to main still rejected with the same error.

**Worker's forensic finding** (via `gh api .../rulesets/rule-suites/...`):

The Phase 4 hardening worker created the ruleset's `required_status_checks` rule with this parameter:
```json
"required_status_checks": [{ "context": "Secret Scan" }]
```

**Missing field: `integration_id`.** When `integration_id` is omitted on a `required_status_checks` rule in a GitHub ruleset, GitHub looks for *legacy commit statuses* (`POST /repos/.../statuses/{sha}`) on the target commit — **not** for check-runs from the Checks API.

The Security Scan workflow produces a *check-run* from `github-actions` (app_id `15368`), not a legacy status. So the ruleset's evaluation looks at legacy statuses on `c2d27e6` (zero present) and fails, even though a passing check-run exists.

Confirmation: `gh api .../commits/c2d27e6/status` returns `{state: "pending", total_count: 0, statuses: []}` — zero legacy statuses. But `.../commits/c2d27e6/check-runs` shows the `Secret Scan` check with `conclusion: success`.

**The fix is a one-field PATCH:** add `"integration_id": 15368` to the rule, then GitHub matches against check-runs from `github-actions`. Everything else stays. Phase 4 worker would have set this if the quirk had been known.

## Root cause is GitHub-design, not config

The PATCH worked cleanly (one-line `integration_id: 15368` added, verified via GET-after) but the push still rejected with the same error. Worker's forensic via rule-suite forensic confirms the check-run on `c2d27e6` (name=Secret Scan, conclusion=success, app.id=15368) is exactly what the rule should match — yet the rule still says "expected."

**The deeper issue:** GitHub's `required_status_checks` rule isn't just matching `check_run.name + app.id`. It's evaluating whether the check is part of a *check_suite associated with the target-ref push event*. The check on `c2d27e6` was created during a `workflow_dispatch` event on the `v5-content-cleanup` branch — its check_suite is associated with that event, not with a hypothetical future main-ref push.

**Catch-22 made explicit:** for `required_status_checks` on `main` to be satisfied, the workflow must have run in the context of a main-targeting event (a push to main, or a PR merging into main). The first sync got through because there was no protection yet. Subsequent direct-push syncs will all hit this same wall by design.

Since this isn't a one-time bug but a structural property of the gate as configured, every future periodic sync from `dstrader-r2 → dstrader-public` will fail the same way unless we change the operational pattern.
